questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(1+\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta )?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, use the identity $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(1+\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ) & =(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(1+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }) \\  & =(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }) \\  & =\frac{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we expand the parentheses in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we rewrite the numerator using $1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{3}⁡x({sec}^{3}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x) & ={cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot {sec}^{3}⁡x-{cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the identity $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot {sec}^{3}⁡x-{cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡x & ={cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})}^{3}-{cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & ={cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cos}^{3}⁡x}-{cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{3}⁡x}{{cos}^{3}⁡x}-\frac{{cos}^{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{cos}^{3}⁡x}}{\cancel{{cos}^{3}⁡x}}-\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡x=1-{cos}^{2}⁡x$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
{cos}^{3}⁡x({sec}^{3}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x)={sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x(\operatorname{csc}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the identity $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}-\frac{2\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =2-2{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡x=1-{cos}^{2}⁡x$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x(\operatorname{csc}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x)=2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡x & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡x \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-\frac{3{sin}^{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{3\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}-\frac{3{sin}^{2}⁡x\cdot \cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =3-3{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3(1-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${cos}^{2}⁡x=1-{sin}^{2}⁡x$  to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
3\operatorname{csc}⁡x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{sin}^{3}⁡x)=3{cos}^{2}⁡x
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since both fractions are over a common denominator, we can add them. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1-2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta $ to simplify the expression in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1-2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator using $1-{cos}^{2}⁡t={sin}^{2}⁡t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t-1}{{cos}^{2}⁡t{tan}^{2}⁡t} & =\frac{-1\cdot (1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )}{{cos}^{2}⁡t{tan}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we rewrite the denominator using the definition of $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta $ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡t} & =\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot {(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot (\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{cos}^{2}⁡t})} \\  & =\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{(\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡t}{{cos}^{2}⁡t})} \\  & =\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{(\frac{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡t}\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡t}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡t}})} \\  & =\frac{-{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{-\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡t}}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡t}} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t-1}{{cos}^{2}⁡t{tan}^{2}⁡t}=-1
$$

$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the expression using the definitions of $\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta $ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta $:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply the numerator and the denominator by $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3(\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }})} \\  & =\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use $1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta $ to simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{3{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}{3\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{1}{3}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }(1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta $ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }(1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta 
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator using $1-{sin}^{2}⁡x={cos}^{2}⁡x.$

$$
\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1}=\frac{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1}
$$

Next, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1} & =\frac{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1} \\  & =-\frac{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cancel{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}}{\cancel{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =-\frac{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{1} \\  & =-(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1}=-(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).
$$

Next, we factor the denominator as difference of squares, and simplify:

$$

$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses and simplify the resulting expression:

$$
3\cos^2 x \left(\sec^2 x -1\right) = 3\cos^2 x \sec^2 x - 3\cos^2 x
$$

Then, we use the identity $\sec x = \dfrac{1}{\cos x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{cos}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-3{cos}^{2}⁡x & =3{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})}^{2}-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{3{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{3\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡x}}-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity $\sin^2 x = 1-\cos^2 x$ to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, as follows:

$$
3(1-\cos^2 x) = 3\cdot \sin^2 x = 3\sin^2 x
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
3\cos^2 x \left(\sec^2 x -1\right)= 3\sin^2 x.
$$

$$
\dfrac{\cos{x}}{1-\cos^2{x}} = \dfrac{\cos{x}}{\sin^2{x}}.
$$

Next, we simplify the expression by separating out the factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{\cos{x}}{1-\cos^2{x}}=\cot{x}\csc{x}.
$$

Then, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify:

$$

$$

$$
\dfrac{\cos^2 x}{1-\sin x} = 1 + \sin x.
